subject: Track editor visual quality usability consistency and creative freedom
type: Review and design proposal; no editor behavior changes
assessment: The native editor already has substantial authoring power. Reaching the AAA target requires clearer interaction, trustworthy visibility, faster composition and a coherent presentation system. Increasing mesh detail alone would leave the main obstacles in place.
strengths_to_preserve: Full-screen native world with a small category rail and contextual palette
Direct road endpoints and geometry handles, seven road families including variable-width splines and bridges
Automatic lap generation and independent untimed practice; do not reintroduce manual waypoints
Free, area and line surface tools, object variants, object runs and seeded Populate preview
Native object photographs and bounded thumbnail caches rather than unrelated illustrative approximations
Undo, retained pending tools, visible save feedback, issue cycling and existing background preparation

priority_definitions.P1: First delivery priorities: difficult-to-see or conflicting interaction, first-use friction, or a large reduction in repetitive authoring
priority_definitions.P2: Subsequent craft and presentation improvements after the core interaction is coherent

findings.finding: Night tracks are extremely difficult to see while editing. Three authored light poles illuminate small islands but leave much of the circuit almost black in the review fixture on both renderers.
findings.recommendation: Default to neutral editor work lighting, with an explicit switch to the actual race lighting. Keep authored lights and race output intact.
findings.acceptance: Road boundaries, selected props and handles remain readable on unlit Night drafts; race preview reproduces the intended actual lighting.

findings.kind: Observed geometry and code-confirmed interaction conflict
findings.finding: The yellow start-direction arrow and a selected straight's yellow confirmation button overlap. Their hit regions intersect, and the start-direction handler runs before road confirmation in the overlapping region.
findings.recommendation: Place contextual controls using collision avoidance, keep them within the usable canvas, and show confirmation only when there is work to confirm. Make start-line controls contextual to start-line selection.
findings.acceptance: No competing gizmo hit areas intersect at short sections, junctions, bridges, screen edges or zoom extremes.

findings.kind: Measured layout concern; physical touch acceptance outstanding
findings.finding: Brush minus/plus controls are 36 by 48 logical units; object categories use 38-unit-high buttons. Production stretching at 960 by 540 reduces a 36-unit width to 27 output pixels. A separate exploratory 960 by 540 logical layout overlaps header/history controls, but that is not the default 1280 by 720 logical layout.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a touch density profile and responsive priorities. Validate target sizes using actual Android density, safe areas and finger spacing. Keep track identity compact and put secondary commands in a labeled menu.
findings.acceptance: Primary touch targets meet at least 48 by 48 Android dp; density conversion is measured rather than assuming Godot units equal dp. Text, handles and all editor modes remain usable on the target phone.

findings.finding: The initial canvas presents an empty field and eight choices without an immediate next-step prompt. Most operating instructions live in a scrolling Help dialog reached through the ellipsis menu. Routine mode hints are assigned to a normally hidden label.
findings.recommendation: Offer Blank plus a few editable starting examples, optional contextual teaching, a short current-tool instruction and a visible explanation for unavailable Test/Publish actions. Keep free creation available from the start.
findings.acceptance: First-time players can place, connect, adjust and test a first loop without verbal coaching. Open roads remain usable for untimed practice where currently allowed.

findings.finding: An already-selected asset must be tapped again to expose variants, size and placement options. Road values are largely on-canvas glyphs, object values use bottom step buttons, and surface settings use a separate right inspector. The object popup reserves a large mostly empty rectangle for simple assets.
findings.recommendation: Use a consistent Properties affordance for every selection, with a compact right panel on larger layouts and a collapsible sheet on phone. Present exact current values, behavior and contextual operations together.
findings.acceptance: Variants and placement modes are discoverable without a tooltip or repeat-tap convention; values and selection survive tool changes.

findings.finding: Teal regular-weight editor controls coexist with yellow condensed menu controls inside Surface options; green Test, yellow on-map actions, illustrated road buttons, native prop photographs and generic line glyphs use inconsistent hierarchy. Copying a selected building uses the generic Objects tree illustration; Layer uses a terrain illustration while actually cycling overlapping roads.
findings.recommendation: Define shared typography, spacing, control heights, focus and selected states, semantic colors and a coherent operation-icon family. Keep actual native asset thumbnails. Rename Layer to describe overlapping-road selection.
findings.acceptance: The same action and state read the same way throughout the editor, including dialogs and disabled controls.

findings.kind: Observed surface terminology and catalog inconsistency
findings.finding: The surface palette still says Grass in Desert and Winter. It provides four prominent choices while the inspector contains seven material choices. Grass/erase mixes a world material with an operation; Water and Puddle have very similar illustrations despite different behavior.
findings.recommendation: Use biome-correct labels and swatches, make erasing explicit, expose one consistent material catalog, and distinguish continuous water from a placed puddle hazard with short behavior descriptions.
findings.acceptance: A player can predict the visual result and driving effect before placing a material in every biome.

findings.finding: Selection and duplication operate on one road/object at a time. The reviewed editor has no exposed multi-selection, reusable prop groups or personal assembly library.
findings.recommendation: Add touch and desktop multi-selection, group transforms and duplication, then reusable local assemblies such as a marshal post, container yard, pit bay or decorated hairpin. Add search and favorites to the asset browser. Groups must retain underlying authored-object and performance accounting.
findings.acceptance: A creator can construct a scene once, reuse it elsewhere and revise the arrangement without repeatedly editing every constituent prop.

findings.finding: Selected objects rotate in 45-degree steps and scale through quarter-step controls. Copy adds a fixed four-metre offset on both axes. Road handles are convenient but exact dimensions are not consistently exposed for ordinary sections.
findings.recommendation: Support optional numeric position/heading/scale and road dimensions, fine/coarse rotation snaps, nudge, align, distribute, mirror and repeat-along-path. Keep direct handles as the primary fast interaction. Show a true-scale vehicle reference for clearance.
findings.acceptance: Creators can deliberately align rows, produce symmetric compositions and match dimensions without repeated trial-and-error drags.

findings.kind: Creative automation opportunity building on existing tools
findings.finding: Populate already previews seeded scenery and exposes Density, Roadside reach and Shuffle. Object runs also exist. There are no exposed local inclusion/exclusion masks, explicit species mixes or persistent editable roadside assemblies in the reviewed interface.
findings.recommendation: Add paintable regions and exclusion zones, biome-coherent scenery recipes, cluster/spacing/scale variation, seed locking, and editable paths for fences and other repeated scenery. Preserve existing hand-placed objects and clearance rules.
findings.acceptance: A creator can place a dense woodland beside one corner, preserve runoff, and make a paddock elsewhere without regenerating or manually repairing the whole map.

findings.finding: The fixed high planning camera supports accurate placement but makes building fronts and vertical relationships hard to judge. The reviewed interface has no explicit clean presentation view or gameplay-camera composition toggle.
findings.recommendation: Provide Plan, Race preview and Clean view. Allow grid/handles/automatic-route direction, collision and bridge-clearance overlays to be switched independently. Race preview must use the approved overhead gameplay framing.
findings.acceptance: A creator can judge silhouette, car clearance, bridge relationships and final race readability without repeatedly entering a full drive.

findings.finding: The shared native assets are a useful coherent starting point, but scattering individual props does not by itself compose a convincing venue. Noisy terrain competes with small props at the planning scale; plain overhead roofs also obscure the quality of the actual models.
findings.recommendation: Create a small set of excellent native venue recipes with track-edge detail, middle-distance storytelling and broad background masses. Add controlled surface edge softness and natural variation where visual and driving boundaries remain honest. Judge props at both planning and race distances before increasing geometry.
findings.acceptance: Several contrasting venues have intentional composition and readable driving lines on phone, using the existing mature restrained art direction and measured budgets.

findings.finding: Test and return-to-editor already exist, and issues can already cycle and focus the offending location. The editor does not expose an integrated spatial review of the last test run.
findings.recommendation: Build on current Test/Edit here with a quick test from a selected position and optional last-run overlays for path, speed, collisions and missed automatic gates. Present practice readiness separately from publication readiness; retain automatic routing.
findings.acceptance: A creator can identify, edit and retry a problematic corner without losing selection, camera or context.

findings.kind: Capacity visibility gap and unmeasured device acceptance
findings.finding: Documents permit 96 road pieces, 96 authored objects and 256 paint strokes. These limits are primarily surfaced by validation messages. Detailed scenes can exhaust the authored-object budget quickly. This visual review did not measure large-map phone frame pacing or memory.
findings.recommendation: Expose understandable live budget counters and warnings before a limit is reached. Profile dense representative scenes before considering separate decorative-instance budgets. Preserve bounded caches, background work and immediate gesture feedback.
findings.acceptance: Supported dense maps remain responsive and stable during prolonged physical-phone editing; group/prefab placement cannot silently bypass validation or budgets.

findings.finding: Publication already requires an eligible tested draft and opens its acknowledged public card. Local sharing offers copied JSON or a file. The editor lacks an exposed final composition and presentation step.
findings.recommendation: Add a concise finish checklist and a clean native hero-image preview, followed by title/description and supported metadata. Improve native sharing and let owners reuse their own assemblies. Any additional sharing metadata or service work needs its own scoped design and contract review.
findings.acceptance: The creator understands what remains before publishing and can present the actual track attractively without external image tools.

recommended_delivery_order.gate: One coherent Road/Surface/Object selection workflow at desktop and phone sizes, without obscured or competing controls
Proposed usability study: first-time players create and test a loop within five minutes without verbal instruction
A creator reuses an authored scene group and decorates selected regions while retaining precise control and visible budgets

recommended_delivery_order.outcome: Polished playable venues ready to share
recommended_delivery_order.gate: Several visually distinct example venues pass moving-view readability, sustained phone performance and owner art review

external_primary_references.supports: Concrete creator-workflow precedent for multi-selection, reusable prefabs, favorites, authored preview conditions and custom event photography
48 by 48 dp minimum touch targets; text contrast and understandable control descriptions
Visible configurable snapping as a precision-authoring precedent

scope_and_limits: Native desktop rendering on the pinned Godot 4.7.2 build using Compatibility/OpenGL and Mobile/Vulkan on RTX 3090; this is not a physical-phone test
All five biomes; 1280 by 720, 960 by 540 physical with production logical scaling, wider output and exploratory 960 by 540 logical layout
27 capture states per final renderer probe, including blank/road/spline/surface/object/population/issues/help and Night with authored lights
Capture/deadline counters are diagnostic completeness checks, not 54 product invariants or a full regression pass
Some actual preparation states may appear in the captures; intermediate loading images are not used to judge final environment art

Concurrent native prop and other project changes were preserved. Source hashes before and after each final probe are in each observations.json; Compatibility reports creator_prop_visual.gd changed on disk during the run. No exact paired pixel or performance equivalence claim is made
Final diagnostic isolates draft, record, account session and cloud-cache storage under the evidence folder and disables the service URL
No owner draft editing, publication, backend write, APK export, installation, deployment, phone input, thermal run, memory profiling or general AAA certification
The review adds an explicit diagnostic and evidence only. The standard dev entry point also refreshes generated build identity files

validation.mobile_command: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/dev.ps1 -Action TestScript -ScriptPath res://tests/review_editor_visuals_2026_10_16.gd -Graphical -RenderingMethod mobile -RenderingDriver vulkan -CommandTimeoutSeconds 240

final_mobile.limitation: VISUAL_REVIEW_COMPLETE printed and all PNGs/observations were saved, but the process did not exit; the standard runner terminated its own process tree at the 240-second command deadline. This is not recorded as a clean passing command, nor attributed to an editor runtime defect without further investigation.

validation.scope: Earlier captures and initial fixture failures are retained in logs. No full Validate, phone acceptance, performance equivalence or physical-device touch test was performed. Review JSON parses successfully; task-specific whitespace check reports no errors.

initial_diagnostic_corrections: Initial sandboxed native launch could not open the normal Godot user log; subsequent native commands received normal Windows resource access through the approval reviewer
An early diagnostic entered the editor before asynchronous app startup completed; its freed-world failure was corrected by waiting for startup_complete
The first selected-road fixture used create_default, whose visible layout contains no editable road pieces. The diagnostic was corrected to build a connected four-piece oval
Additional waits cover serial thumbnail rendering and population scene preparation; these do not change runtime behavior
